```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5, dpi = 150)
library(tidyverse); library(scales); library(knitr)
# Paths are relative to the project root (one level above /code)
root <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), ".."))

```

# 1. Question and scope

**Empirical question.** On 7 October 2026 the First Committee adopted its programme of work by recorded vote after rejecting a Russian amendment on speaking-time limits. Is a recorded vote on organizational matters unusual, and what does the pattern of support for Russia's procedural positions reveal about alignment — in particular whether China and India behave differently on procedural questions than on substantive ones?

**Data provenance** (all files in `/data`, every row traceable):

* 2026: UN press release GA/DIS/3764 (tallies and named "against"/"abstaining" states), GA/DIS/3762 (5 October debate), UN Transcripts (ASR, *not official*) for meetings 1–3 of the 81st session. Verbatim records A/C.1/81/PV.1–3 were **not yet available** on ODS when checked (10 Oct 2026).
* Baseline: all First Committee verbatim records (A/C.1/73/PV.x – A/C.1/79/PV.x) retrievable from the UN Official Document System (ODS) API; recorded votes parsed automatically by `code/parse_pv.py` and validated against official totals.
* Plenary context: Voeten/Bailey–Strezhnev–Voeten dyadic agreement scores (Harvard Dataverse, doi:10.7910/DVN/LEJUQZ, `AgreementScores.csv`, 1946–2024).

# 2. Load and validate data

```{r load}
items <- read_csv(dd("fc_vote_items_raw.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
votes <- read_csv(dd("fc_votes_long_raw.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
cls   <- read_csv(dd("procedural_classification.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
ref   <- read_csv(dd("country_reference.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
i26   <- read_csv(dd("fc2026_vote_items.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
v26   <- read_csv(dd("fc2026_votes_known.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
voe   <- read_csv(dd("voeten_agreement_pairs_2000_2024.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

val <- items %>% count(session, valid) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = valid, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  rename(valid = `1`, failed_validation = `0`)
kable(val, caption = "Parsed recorded votes per session; 'valid' = parsed country counts equal the official totals printed in the verbatim record")
items_v <- items %>% filter(valid == 1) %>%
  left_join(cls, by = "vote_id") %>%
  mutate(category = replace_na(category, "substantive"))
votes_v <- votes %>% semi_join(items_v, by = "vote_id") %>% left_join(items_v %>% select(vote_id, year, category), by = "vote_id")
cat("Validated votes:", nrow(items_v), " | country-vote records:", nrow(votes_v), "\n")
kable(count(items_v, category), caption = "Validated votes by category")
```

Session 79 (2024) has only a handful of verbatim records on ODS (the action-phase records are not retrievable), and **no First Committee verbatim records exist on ODS for session 80 (2025)**; the 2025 baseline therefore relies on UN Transcripts (the programme of work was adopted without objection on 3 October 2025, and the 2026 programme of work was adopted without objection on 6 November 2025 under document A/C.1/80/CRP.4).

# 3. Descriptive tallies: the two 2026 votes

```{r tallies2026}
kable(i26 %>% select(vote_id, object, proposer, vote_requested_by, yes, no, abs, outcome, country_lists_published))
t26 <- i26 %>% transmute(vote = c("Russian amendment\n(speaking times)", "Programme of work\nA/C.1/81/CRP.1"), Yes = yes, No = no, Abstain = abs,
                         `Not recorded` = 193 - yes - no - abs) %>%
  pivot_longer(-vote, names_to = "choice", values_to = "n") %>% mutate(choice = factor(choice, levels = names(pal)))
g1 <- ggplot(t26, aes(x = vote, y = n, fill = choice)) + geom_col(width = .6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), position = position_stack(vjust = .5), size = 4, family = "serif") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) + coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Figure 1. The two recorded procedural votes in the First Committee, 7 October 2026",
       subtitle = "Programme of work: against = Burkina Faso, DPRK, Iran, Mali, Nicaragua, Niger, Russia;\nabstaining = Algeria, Central African Republic, China, Congo, India. Amendment: no country lists published yet.",
       x = NULL, y = "Number of UN member states (193)", fill = NULL,
       caption = "Source: UN press release GA/DIS/3764; UN Transcripts, 81st session, 3rd meeting. 'Not recorded' = not voting or absent.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(fd("fig1_2026_tallies.png"), g1, width = 9.5, height = 4.8, dpi = 200); g1
```

On the programme of work, `r 135+7+5` states voted; Russia's 7-state "no" coalition combined Russia with Iran, the DPRK, Nicaragua and the three Alliance of Sahel States (AES) members; China and India abstained. The 15 states that backed the Russian amendment are not yet identifiable from published sources.

# 4. Historical baseline: how rare are procedural recorded votes?

```{r baseline}
proc <- items_v %>% filter(category != "substantive") %>%
  left_join(votes_v %>% filter(country %in% c("Russian Federation","China","India","United States of America")) %>%
              select(vote_id, country, vote) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = country, values_from = vote), by = "vote_id") %>%
  transmute(year, meeting_date, category, description, proposer, yes = parsed_yes, no = parsed_no, abs = parsed_abs,
            Russia = `Russian Federation`, China, India, USA = `United States of America`)
p26 <- tibble(year = 2026, meeting_date = "7 October 2026", category = "procedural",
              description = c("Russian amendment to footnote b of A/C.1/81/CRP.1 (speaking times)", "Adoption of programme of work A/C.1/81/CRP.1 (vote requested by the United States)"),
              proposer = c("Russian Federation","Chair/Bureau"), yes = c(15,135), no = c(63,7), abs = c(56,5),
              Russia = c("(not published)","No"), China = c("(not published)","Abstain"), India = c("(not published)","Abstain"), USA = c("(not published)","(Yes or not voting; not published)"))
proc_all <- bind_rows(proc, p26)
write_csv(proc_all, file.path(root, "output", "table_procedural_votes_2018_2026.csv"))
kable(proc_all, caption = "All First Committee procedural/organizational recorded votes found, 2018–2026")
share <- items_v %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(all_recorded = n(), procedural_core = sum(category == "procedural"),
                                                  machinery_procedural = sum(category == "machinery_procedural"))
kable(share, caption = "Validated recorded votes per year (2024: only organizational-phase records retrievable)")
```

# 5. Pairwise agreement: procedural vs substantive

Agreement index (Lijphart 1963, the same construction as Voeten's dyadic scores): 1 = identical vote, 0.5 = one abstains and the other votes yes/no, 0 = opposite votes; votes where either state did not vote are dropped. "Identical" is the share of exactly matching votes.

```{r pairs}
ag <- function(a, b) case_when(a == b ~ 1, a == "Abstain" | b == "Abstain" ~ .5, TRUE ~ 0)
pairs <- tribble(~c1, ~c2,
  "China","Russian Federation", "India","Russian Federation", "China","India", "Belarus","Russian Federation",
  "Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Russian Federation", "United States of America","Russian Federation",
  "China","United States of America", "India","United States of America", "Brazil","Russian Federation", "South Africa","Russian Federation")
wide <- votes_v %>% select(vote_id, country, vote) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = country, values_from = vote)
cat_of <- items_v %>% select(vote_id, category, year)
pair_tab <- pmap_dfr(pairs, function(c1, c2) {
  wide %>% select(vote_id, a = all_of(c1), b = all_of(c2)) %>% filter(!is.na(a), !is.na(b)) %>%
    left_join(cat_of, by = "vote_id") %>%
    mutate(cat2 = recode(category, substantive = "Substantive FC votes 2018-23", procedural = "Core procedural FC votes 2018-24 (n<=7)",
                         machinery_procedural = "UNDC/visa procedural decisions 2019-20 (n=11)")) %>%
    group_by(cat2) %>% summarise(n = n(), agreement = mean(ag(a, b)), identical = mean(a == b), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pair = paste(c1, "–", c2))
})
ukey <- function(a, b) paste(pmin(a, b), pmax(a, b))
pl <- voe %>% filter(year >= 2018) %>% mutate(key = ukey(country1, country2)) %>% group_by(key) %>% summarise(agreement = mean(agree), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(cat2 = "UNGA plenary, all recorded votes 2018-24 (Voeten; mean of yearly scores)")
pair_tab <- pair_tab %>% mutate(key = ukey(str_split_fixed(pair, " – ", 2)[,1], str_split_fixed(pair, " – ", 2)[,2]))
pair_all <- bind_rows(pair_tab, pl %>% inner_join(pair_tab %>% distinct(key, pair), by = "key")) %>% select(pair, cat2, n, agreement, identical)
write_csv(pair_all, file.path(root, "output", "table_pairwise_agreement.csv"))
kable(pair_all %>% arrange(pair, cat2) %>% mutate(across(c(agreement, identical), ~round(., 3))), caption = "Pairwise agreement by vote type")
short <- function(x) x %>% str_replace_all("Russian Federation","Russia") %>% str_replace_all("United States of America","USA") %>% str_replace_all("Iran \\(Islamic Republic of\\)","Iran")
g3 <- pair_all %>% mutate(pair = short(pair), pair = fct_reorder(pair, agreement, .fun = function(x) x[1])) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = agreement, y = pair, colour = cat2, shape = cat2)) + geom_point(size = 3.4, alpha = .9) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = percent) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#d7301f", "#2b8cbe", "grey40", "#fdae61")) +
  labs(title = "Figure 3. China votes with Russia on procedure even more than on substance; India does not",
       subtitle = "Lijphart agreement index (1 = identical, 0.5 = one abstains, 0 = opposite)",
       x = "Agreement", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
       caption = "Sources: First Committee verbatim records A/C.1/73–79/PV.x (validated recorded votes); Voeten dyadic agreement scores (Harvard Dataverse).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
ggsave(fd("fig3_pairwise_agreement.png"), g3, width = 9.5, height = 6.5, dpi = 200); g3
```

```{r china_india_detail}
sel_c <- c("Russian Federation","China","India","Belarus","Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Syrian Arab Republic","Cuba","Nicaragua","Democratic People’s Republic of Korea","Mali","Burkina Faso","Niger","Algeria","Brazil","South Africa","Egypt","Indonesia","United States of America")
detail <- items_v %>% filter(category != "substantive") %>% select(vote_id, year, description) %>% crossing(country = sel_c) %>%
  left_join(votes_v %>% filter(country %in% c("Russian Federation","China","India","Belarus","Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Syrian Arab Republic","Cuba","Nicaragua","Democratic People’s Republic of Korea","Mali","Burkina Faso","Niger","Algeria","Brazil","South Africa","Egypt","Indonesia","United States of America")) %>% select(vote_id, country, vote), by = c("vote_id","country"))
d26 <- tibble(vote_id = "FC81_CRP1", year = 2026, description = "Adoption of programme of work A/C.1/81/CRP.1") %>%
  crossing(country = unique(detail$country)) %>% left_join(v26 %>% select(vote_id, country, vote), by = c("vote_id","country")) %>%
  mutate(vote = replace_na(vote, "Yes or not voting (unpublished)"))
lv <- c("Yes","Abstain","No","Not voting","Yes or not voting (unpublished)")
heat <- bind_rows(detail, d26) %>% mutate(vote = replace_na(vote, "Not voting"),
  short = paste0(year, " ", str_trunc(description, 48)), country = short(country) %>% str_replace("Democratic People’s Republic of Korea","DPRK") %>% str_replace("Syrian Arab Republic","Syria"))
ord <- bind_rows(detail, d26) %>% distinct(vote_id, year, description) %>% arrange(year, vote_id) %>% mutate(short = paste0(year, " ", str_trunc(description, 48)))
heat <- heat %>% mutate(short = factor(short, levels = unique(ord$short)), vote = factor(vote, levels = lv),
  country = factor(country, levels = rev(c("Russia","Belarus","Iran","DPRK","Syria","Nicaragua","Cuba","Mali","Burkina Faso","Niger","China","India","Algeria","Egypt","Indonesia","Brazil","South Africa","USA"))))
g4 <- ggplot(heat, aes(x = short, y = country, fill = vote)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Yes = "#2b8cbe", Abstain = "#fdae61", No = "#d7301f", `Not voting` = "grey55", `Yes or not voting (unpublished)` = "#c6dbef"), drop = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Figure 4. Who stood where on procedural votes, 2018–2026", subtitle = "Votes are as cast on each motion/decision (a 'Yes' on the 2020 division motion was a vote against Russia's position)",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "Sources: A/C.1/73–79/PV.x; GA/DIS/3764 (2026: only 'against' and 'abstaining' published).") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, size = 7.5), legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(fd("fig4_procedural_heatmap.png"), g4, width = 12, height = 7.5, dpi = 200); g4
```

# 6. Regional and coalition breakdowns

For each procedural vote: does a bloc member vote the same way as Russia, the opposite way, abstain, or not vote? Membership: UN regional groups; NAM (2026 list; Chile counted as member until 2025, South Sudan from 2024); EU-27 (UK counted only as non-EU; votes before 31 Jan 2020 for the UK are excluded from the EU bloc for simplicity, i.e., EU-27 used throughout); AES = Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger.

```{r blocs}
ref2 <- ref %>% mutate(bloc_regional = un_regional_group)
rus <- votes_v %>% filter(country == "Russian Federation") %>% select(vote_id, rus = vote)
procids <- items_v %>% filter(category != "substantive") %>% pull(vote_id)
member_rows <- function(bloc, members, ids, nam_adj = FALSE) {
  crossing(vote_id = ids, country = members) %>% left_join(votes_v %>% select(vote_id, country, vote), by = c("vote_id","country")) %>%
    left_join(rus, by = "vote_id") %>% left_join(items_v %>% select(vote_id, year), by = "vote_id") %>% mutate(bloc = bloc)
}
nam_hist <- c(ref$country[ref$nam_2026 == 1], "Chile")
blocs <- bind_rows(
  member_rows("Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger (AES since 2023)", ref$country[ref$aes_sahel == 1], procids),
  member_rows("NAM", nam_hist, procids) %>% filter(!(country == "South Sudan" & year < 2024)),
  member_rows("EU-27 member states", ref$country[ref$eu27 == 1], procids),
  member_rows("African Group", ref$country[ref$un_regional_group == "African Group"], procids),
  member_rows("Asia-Pacific Group", ref$country[ref$un_regional_group == "Asia and the Pacific Group"], procids),
  member_rows("GRULAC", ref$country[str_detect(ref$un_regional_group, "GRULAC")], procids),
  member_rows("Eastern European Group (excl. Russia)", setdiff(ref$country[ref$un_regional_group == "Eastern European Group"], "Russian Federation"), procids),
  member_rows("WEOG (+US)", ref$country[str_detect(ref$un_regional_group, "WEOG")], procids)) %>%
  mutate(rel = case_when(is.na(vote) ~ "Not voting", vote == rus ~ "Same as Russia", vote == "Abstain" ~ "Abstain", rus == "Abstain" ~ "Yes/No while Russia abstained", TRUE ~ "Opposite to Russia"))
bt <- blocs %>% count(bloc, rel) %>% group_by(bloc) %>% mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()
kable(bt %>% select(-n) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = rel, values_from = share, values_fill = 0) %>% mutate(across(-bloc, ~percent(., .1))),
      caption = "Bloc members' votes relative to Russia on procedural votes 2018–2024 (pooled member-votes)")
write_csv(bt, file.path(root, "output", "table_bloc_relative_to_russia.csv"))
g5 <- bt %>% mutate(rel = factor(rel, levels = c("Same as Russia","Abstain","Yes/No while Russia abstained","Opposite to Russia","Not voting"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = share, y = fct_rev(bloc), fill = rel)) + geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Same as Russia` = "#7a0177", Abstain = "#fdae61", `Yes/No while Russia abstained` = "#bdbdbd", `Opposite to Russia` = "#2b8cbe", `Not voting` = "grey85")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "Figure 5. Procedural votes 2018–2024: bloc members relative to Russia's vote", subtitle = "Pooled member-votes, 18 validated procedural votes. Outside Europe, abstention and non-participation dominate; EU/WEOG members mostly vote against Russia",
       x = "Share of member-votes", y = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "Sources: A/C.1/73–79/PV.x; group membership as documented in data/country_reference.csv") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(fd("fig5_blocs_relative_to_russia.png"), g5, width = 10, height = 5.5, dpi = 200); g5
```

```{r aes_2026}
b26 <- ref %>% left_join(v26 %>% select(country, vote), by = "country") %>% mutate(vote = replace_na(vote, "Yes or not voting"))
kable(bind_rows(
  b26 %>% filter(aes_sahel == 1) %>% count(vote) %>% mutate(bloc = "AES"),
  b26 %>% filter(nam_2026 == 1) %>% count(vote) %>% mutate(bloc = "NAM (2026)"),

```

**EU cohesion.** On every validated procedural vote, did all EU-27 member states that voted cast the same vote?

```{r eu}
eu <- votes_v %>% filter(country %in% ref$country[ref$eu27 == 1]) %>% group_by(vote_id, category) %>%
  summarise(n_voting = n(), modal_share = max(table(vote)) / n(), .groups = "drop")
kable(eu %>% group_by(category) %>% summarise(votes = n(), mean_modal_share = mean(modal_share), fully_cohesive = mean(modal_share == 1)),
      caption = "EU-27 member-state cohesion (share voting with the EU modal choice); similarity is not evidence of formal EU coordination")
```

# 7. Plenary context (Voeten)

```{r voeten}
vs <- voe %>% filter(paste(country1, country2) %in% c("China Russian Federation","India Russian Federation","China India","United States of America Russian Federation","China United States of America","India United States of America")) %>%
  mutate(pair = short(paste(country1, "–", country2)))
g6 <- ggplot(vs, aes(year, agree, colour = pair)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Figure 6. UNGA plenary voting agreement, 2000–2024", subtitle = "China–Russia c. 78–85% and India–Russia c. 60–70% in 2020–24; US–Russia c. 24–34%",
       x = NULL, y = "Agreement (Lijphart index)", colour = NULL, caption = "Source: Bailey, Strezhnev & Voeten, UNGA Ideal Points dataset, AgreementScores.csv (Harvard Dataverse, doi:10.7910/DVN/LEJUQZ).") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
ggsave(fd("fig6_voeten_plenary_agreement.png"), g6, width = 10, height = 5.2, dpi = 200); g6
kable(vs %>% filter(year >= 2020) %>% select(pair, year, agree) %>% mutate(agree = round(agree, 3)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = agree))
```

# 8. Limitations and alternative explanations

* **2026 country-level data are incomplete.** Only the 7 "against" and 5 "abstaining" states on CRP.1 are named; the 135 "in favour" and every country position on the amendment are not yet published (A/C.1/81/PV.3 not on ODS as of 10 Oct 2026). 46 member states did not vote on CRP.1.
* **Small N.** 18 validated procedural votes 2018–2024 (8 Russian-initiated/backed), plus 2 in 2026. Agreement on procedural votes rests on few observations and is sensitive to the visa-linked UNDC cluster of 2019–2020.
* **Coverage gaps.** 22 of 651 parsed votes failed validation and were dropped (all substantive). Session 79 action-phase and all session 80 verbatim records are not on ODS. Procedural votes outside the parsed PVs (2024 action phase, 2025) could exist; UN Transcripts for 2025 meetings show none, but several 2025 transcripts are missing.
* **Abstention as signalling.** An abstention can mean sympathy without cost, hedging, instructions not received, or objection to the *manner* (a vote) rather than the content. China spoke for Russia's position on 5 October but abstained on 7 October; the Chair did not allow explanations of vote, so motives are not on record.
* **Procedural salience.** Speaking-time limits matter more to large delegations with long statements and to small delegations struggling to cover meetings; voting may reflect these interests rather than geopolitical alignment.
* **Voting together ≠ coordination.** Identical votes of the AES states or of EU members do not prove coordination; the EU is an observer and does not vote in the Committee.
* **Correlation ≠ causation.** No claim is made that Russia's lobbying caused any vote.

# 9. Reproduction

1. `python3 code/parse_pv.py data/raw_pv data` (needs poppler `pdftotext`/`pdfinfo`) regenerates `fc_vote_items_raw.csv` and `fc_votes_long_raw.csv` from the stored PDFs (downloaded from `https://documents.un.org/api/symbol/access?s=<symbol>&l=en&t=pdf`).
2. `python3 code/build_ref.py` and `python3 code/make_2026_and_classification.py` rebuild reference and hand-coded tables.
3. `Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("code/analysis.Rmd", output_dir = "output")'`.
